claim: In Drosophila, the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster dopamine neurons mediate reward signals.
source: In Drosophila, the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster dopamine neurons mediate reward signals.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about the PAM neurons.

claim: Localized inhibitory input to the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons titrates olfactory reward memory.
source: Here, we show that localized inhibitory input to the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons titrates olfactory reward memory and controls memory specificity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Localized inhibitory input to the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons controls memory specificity.
source: Here, we show that localized inhibitory input to the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons titrates olfactory reward memory and controls memory specificity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by generalization experiments in Figure 4.

claim: The inhibitory regulation of PAM neurons was mediated by metabotropic gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors clustered in presynaptic microdomain of the PAM boutons.
source: The inhibitory regulation was mediated by metabotropic gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors clustered in presynaptic microdomain of the PAM boutons.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi experiments (Figure 1A) and localization studies (Figure 2B).

claim: Cell type-specific silencing of GABA receptors enhanced memory by augmenting internal reward signals.
source: Cell type-specific silencing the GABA receptors enhanced memory by augmenting internal reward signals.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data (Figure 1A-B) and calcium imaging showing increased sugar responses (Figure 1F-H).

claim: The disruption of GABA signaling reduced memory specificity to the rewarded odor by changing local odor representations in the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons.
source: Strikingly, the disruption of GABA signaling reduced memory specificity to the rewarded odor by changing local odor representations in the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons.
evidence: This is supported by odor generalization experiments (Figure 4A-D) and calcium imaging of odor responses (Figure 3D-E).

claim: Maladaptive presynaptic regulation causes optimistic cognitive bias.
source: Maladaptive presynaptic regulation causes optimistic cognitive bias.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the behavioral phenotypes observed (enhanced memory and reduced specificity) and comparison to optimism literature.

claim: Dopamine neurons are primarily involved in reward processing across animal phyla.
source: Across animal phyla, dopamine neurons are primarily involved in reward processing (Brembs et al., 2002; Tobler et al., 2005; Liu et al., 2012; Ichinose et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A subset of dopamine neurons in the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster mediates the reinforcement property of sugar reward in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: In the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, a subset of dopamine neurons in the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster mediates the reinforcement property of sugar reward (Burke et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Dopamine input to the mushroom body causes changes in preference of a simultaneously presented odor by modulating the output of Kenyon cells.
source: In olfactory learning, dopamine input to the mushroom body (MB) causes changes in preference of a simultaneously presented odor by modulating the output of odor-representing MB intrinsic neurons, Kenyon cells (KCs) (Séjourné et al., 2011; Boto et al., 2014; Cohn et al., 2015; Owald et al., 2015; Louis et al., 2018; Hige et al., 2015; Bilz et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Associative presentations of odor and electric shocks change the activity of MB-projecting dopamine neurons.
source: Such associative presentations of odor and electric shocks were reported to change the activity of MB-projecting dopamine neurons (Riemensperger et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Axon terminals of dopamine neurons locally integrate olfactory inputs to function as multiple independent units.
source: Recent studies (Hattori et al., 2017; Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2017; Takemura et al., 2017) suggest that axon terminals of the dopamine neurons locally integrate olfactory inputs to function as multiple independent units, though such subcellular reward processing has yet to be examined.
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies, though the authors note it has not been fully examined.

claim: Six GABA receptor genes are identified in the fly genome.
source: Six GABA receptor genes are identified in the fly genome.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Drosophila genetics.

claim: Downregulation of GABA-B-R3 in PAM neurons increases appetitive olfactory memory performance.
source: We found increased memory performance by downregulation of a metabotropic GABA receptor, GABA-B-R3 (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1A and supplementary figures.

claim: Acute silencing of GABA-B-R3 in PAM neurons using Tub-GAL80ts enhances appetitive memory performance.
source: Consistently, adult stage-specific GABA-B-R3 silencing in the PAM neurons using Tub-GAL80ts (McGuire et al., 2003) similarly enhanced appetitive memory performance (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data in Figure 1B using temporal control of gene expression.

claim: GABA-B-R3 is expressed broadly in the brain, including the majority of the PAM cluster neurons.
source: GABA-B-R3 was expressed broadly in the brain, including the majority of the PAM cluster neurons (Figure 1C–D), whereas the expression was weak in KCs (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by expression analysis using CRIMIC insertion shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: GABA-B-R3 expression is weak in Kenyon cells.
source: GABA-B-R3 was expressed broadly in the brain, including the majority of the PAM cluster neurons (Figure 1C–D), whereas the expression was weak in KCs (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by expression analysis shown in Figure 1D and supplementary figure.

claim: There was no notable morphological alteration in the brain of GABA-B-R3 knock-down flies.
source: There was no notable morphological alteration in the brain of knock-down flies (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation, though data is not shown.

claim: The performance of R58E02-GAL4/UAS-GABA-B-R3-RNAi flies reached a significantly higher asymptote than control genotypes without changing the acquisition speed.
source: The performance of R58E02-GAL4/UAS-GABA-B-R3-RNAi flies reached a significantly higher asymptote than control genotypes without changing the acquisition speed (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is supported by memory acquisition curve analysis shown in Figure 1E and supplementary figures.

claim: In learning theory, the magnitude of reinforcement is the determinant for the plateau of the acquisition curve.
source: In a learning theory, the magnitude of reinforcement is the determinant for the plateau of the acquisition curve (Rescorla, 1972), suggesting that sugar reward was perceived more strongly with enhanced dopaminergic activity in the GABA-B-R3 knock-down flies.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to learning theory literature.

claim: Sugar reward was perceived more strongly with enhanced dopaminergic activity in the GABA-B-R3 knock-down flies.
source: In a learning theory, the magnitude of reinforcement is the determinant for the plateau of the acquisition curve (Rescorla, 1972), suggesting that sugar reward was perceived more strongly with enhanced dopaminergic activity in the GABA-B-R3 knock-down flies.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased asymptote in acquisition curves and supported by learning theory.

claim: Downregulating GABA-B-R3 augments sugar responses in PAM-γ5 and PAM-α1 neurons.
source: Live calcium imaging at terminal branches of the reward-related PAM neurons (i.e., PAM-γ5 and -α1) revealed the augmented sugar responses upon downregulating GABA-B-R3 (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: GABA-B-R3 signaling is required for negative regulation of sugar reward.
source: We thus conclude that GABA-B-R3 signaling is required for negative regulation of the sugar reward.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the behavioral and calcium imaging data presented.

claim: GABA-B-R3 proteins are heavily localized to the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons.
source: GABA-B-R3 proteins were heavily localized to the presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons (Figure 2A–B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by imaging of GFP-tagged GABA-B-R3 shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: A single pair of GABAergic anterior paired lateral (APL) neurons massively innervate the entire mushroom body.
source: A single pair of the GABAergic anterior paired lateral (APL) neurons was reported to massively innervate the entire MB and to be involved in olfactory learning (Liu and Davis, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: APL neurons are involved in olfactory learning.
source: A single pair of the GABAergic anterior paired lateral (APL) neurons was reported to massively innervate the entire MB and to be involved in olfactory learning (Liu and Davis, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: PAM and APL neuron ramifications abut on each other.
source: Differential labeling of the PAM and APL neurons revealed that their ramifications abut on each other (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is supported by double labeling imaging shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: Knock-down of Gad1 in APL neurons enhances reward memory.
source: Consistently, we found enhanced reward memory in knock-down flies for glutamic acid decarboxylase 1 (Gad1) and vesicular GABA transporter (VGAT) in the APL neuron (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Knock-down of VGAT in APL neurons enhances reward memory.
source: Consistently, we found enhanced reward memory in knock-down flies for glutamic acid decarboxylase 1 (Gad1) and vesicular GABA transporter (VGAT) in the APL neuron (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The enhanced calcium activity upon GABA-B-R3 knock-down is much more pronounced in the presynaptic terminals than in dendrites of PAM neurons.
source: The enhanced calcium activity upon GABA-B-R3 knock-down was much more pronounced in the presynaptic terminals (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This is supported by volumetric calcium imaging comparing dendrites and terminals shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: GABAergic signals from APL neurons negatively control reward gain at the output site of PAM neurons through GABA-B-R3 signaling in the mushroom body.
source: Therefore, GABAergic signals from the APL neurons negatively control the reward gain at the output site of the PAM neurons through GABA-B-R3 signaling in the MB.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the localization, connectivity, and functional data presented.

claim: Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry sensor is composed of GCaMP fused to calcium insensitive mCherry and targeted to active zones.
source: This sensor is composed of GCaMP fused to calcium insensitive mCherry and targeted to active zones using the short fragment of Brp, enabling the measurement of local calcium influx at active zones (Kiragasi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing the sensor.

claim: Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry enables measurement of local calcium influx at active zones.
source: This sensor is composed of GCaMP fused to calcium insensitive mCherry and targeted to active zones using the short fragment of Brp, enabling the measurement of local calcium influx at active zones (Kiragasi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing the sensor's function.

claim: Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry localizes to active zones of PAM neurons in the mushroom body.
source: Immunolabelling confirmed the localization of the sensor proteins to active zones of the PAM neurons in the MB (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 3A and supplementary figure.

claim: Active zone calcium in PAM terminals shows large heterogeneity among active zones.
source: Live imaging of punctate Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry signals in the PAM terminals visualized a large heterogeneity of calcium levels among active zones (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B and supplementary figures.

claim: Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry signals have temporal fluctuations, which are amplified by silencing GABA-B-R3.
source: Furthermore, we found that Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry signals had temporal fluctuations, which was amplified by silencing GABA-B-R3 (Figure 3B and Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by temporal analysis of calcium signals shown in Figure 3B-C.

claim: GABA-B-R3 in PAM terminals stabilizes basal presynaptic activity.
source: GABA-B-R3 in the PAM terminals may thus stabilize the basal presynaptic activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased temporal fluctuations upon GABA-B-R3 knockdown.

claim: GABA inhibition contributes to the robustness of activity against local perturbations.
source: This suggests that GABA inhibition contributes to the robustness of activity against local perturbations.
evidence: This is inferred from the stabilization of basal activity by GABA-B-R3.

claim: System robustness is often related to refined regulation of activity patterns by which information is efficiently coded.
source: System robustness is often related to refined regulation of activity patterns by which information is efficiently coded (Hesse and Gross, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work on system robustness.

claim: In control flies, odor presentations barely changed the distribution of active-zone calcium with a marginal increase of the overall signal intensity.
source: In control flies, odor presentations barely changed the distribution of active-zone calcium with a marginal increase of the overall signal intensity (Figure 3D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3D-E.

claim: Sugar ingestion induced global presynaptic calcium increase and decreased signal heterogeneity in control flies.
source: In contrast, sugar ingestion induced global presynaptic calcium increase and decreased the signal heterogeneity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in supplementary figure.

claim: GABA-B-R3 knock-down flies responded to olfactory stimulation much more strongly than controls.
source: Strikingly, GABA-B-R3 knock-down flies responded to an olfactory stimulation much more strongly (Figure 3D–E), as if in response to a global sugar stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3D-E.

claim: The average peak area (cluster size) of Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry signals became larger upon knocking down GABA-B-R3 both before and during odor stimulation.
source: We found that the average peak area (i.e., cluster size) became larger upon knocking down GABA-B-R3 both before and during the odor stimulation (Figure 3F–G).
evidence: This is supported by spatial analysis of calcium signals shown in Figure 3F-G.

claim: KC and PAM terminals form mutual synapses in the mushroom body lobe.
source: Since KC and PAM terminals form mutual synapses in the MB lobe (Takemura et al., 2017; Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2017), the overall disinhibition in the knock-down terminals may impair the selective delivery of dopaminergic reward signals to odor-activated KCs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior anatomical studies.

claim: Overall disinhibition in knock-down PAM terminals may impair the selective delivery of dopaminergic reward signals to odor-activated KCs.
source: Since KC and PAM terminals form mutual synapses in the MB lobe (Takemura et al., 2017; Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2017), the overall disinhibition in the knock-down terminals may impair the selective delivery of dopaminergic reward signals to odor-activated KCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical connectivity and the observed spatial changes in calcium signals.

claim: Conditioned odor approach of wild-type flies drops by increasing the blend ratio of a contaminant odor to the trained odor.
source: Conditioned odor approach of wild-type flies drops by increasing the blend ratio of a contaminant odor to the trained odor (Ichinose et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior behavioral studies.

claim: Downregulation of GABA-B-R3 in PAM neurons results in a broader generalization profile.
source: Strikingly, the downregulation of GABA-B-R3 in the PAM neurons resulted in a broader generalization profile, indicating that reward memory in the knock-down flies is less specific to the learned odor (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by odor generalization behavioral data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Reward memory in GABA-B-R3 knock-down flies is less specific to the learned odor.
source: Strikingly, the downregulation of GABA-B-R3 in the PAM neurons resulted in a broader generalization profile, indicating that reward memory in the knock-down flies is less specific to the learned odor (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is inferred from the broader generalization profile observed in behavioral experiments.

claim: Downregulating GAD1 expression in APL neurons results in broadened generalization profiles.
source: Moreover, we found similarly broadened generalization profiles by downregulating GAD1 expression in the APL neurons (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is supported by odor generalization behavioral data shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: Local GABAergic inhibition of PAM neurons regulates the intensity and specificity of reward memory.
source: We altogether conclude that local GABAergic inhibition of the PAM neurons regulates the intensity and specificity of reward memory (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on all the behavioral and physiological data presented.

claim: Presynaptic modulation of PAM neurons is a critical component for determining the magnitude of dopaminergic reward signals.
source: Our results indicate that presynaptic modulation of the PAM neurons is a critical component for determining the magnitude of dopaminergic reward signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing enhanced reward responses upon GABA-B-R3 knockdown.

claim: Abolition of local GABAergic input to PAM terminals enhanced internal reward intensity.
source: Notably, abolition of the local GABAergic input to the PAM terminals not only enhanced the internal reward intensity but compromised memory specificity (Figures 1 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: Abolition of local GABAergic input to PAM terminals compromised memory specificity.
source: Notably, abolition of the local GABAergic input to the PAM terminals not only enhanced the internal reward intensity but compromised memory specificity (Figures 1 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: GABA-B-R3 has a dual physiological role: gain control and spatial segmentation of dopaminergic reward signals in PAM terminals.
source: These behavioral alterations can be explained by a dual physiological role of GABA-B-R3, that is, the gain control and the spatial segmentation of dopaminergic reward signals in the PAM terminals (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined behavioral and physiological data.

claim: The behavioral traits caused by downregulation of GABA-B-R3 are characteristic of optimism.
source: As the behavioral traits caused by the downregulation of GABA-B-R3 are characteristic in optimism (Carver et al., 2010; Solvi et al., 2016), presynaptic control of reward signals may underlie such a cognitive bias.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison to optimism literature cited.

claim: Presynaptic control of reward signals may underlie cognitive bias such as optimism.
source: As the behavioral traits caused by the downregulation of GABA-B-R3 are characteristic in optimism (Carver et al., 2010; Solvi et al., 2016), presynaptic control of reward signals may underlie such a cognitive bias.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed behavioral phenotypes and literature on optimism.

claim: Similar subcellular modulation of punishment-mediating neurons may conversely lead to pessimistic bias.
source: It would be fruitful to examine if a similar subcellular modulation of punishment-mediating neurons conversely leads to the pessimistic bias (Sharot et al., 2009; Bateson et al., 2011; Sharot et al., 2012; Kregiel et al., 2016; Solvi et al., 2016; Zidar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion for future research based on the current findings.

claim: The T2A self-cleaving peptide allows bi-cistronic translation by a ribosome skipping mechanism.
source: The T2A self-cleaving peptide between the target protein and GAL4 allows bi-cistronic translation by a ribosome skipping mechanism (Diao and White, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing the T2A mechanism.

claim: Without transgene induction, appetitive memory of Tub-GAL80ts flies was indistinguishable from controls.
source: Without transgene induction, their appetitive memory was indistinguishable from the controls (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Active-zone calcium in PAM terminals is likely to reflect local input in the mushroom body.
source: As active-zone calcium in the PAM terminals is likely to reflect local input in the MB (see Figure 2G and H), we hypothesized that GABA-B-R3 controls the spatial representation of odor information in the PAM terminals.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential responses in dendrites vs terminals shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: Stimulus-specific presynaptic responses reflect differential input sites of odor and sugar signals (pre- and post-synaptic sites of PAM neurons, respectively).
source: These stimulus-specific presynaptic responses are likely to reflect differential input sites of odor and sugar signals, that is, pre- and post-synaptic sites of the PAM neurons, respectively.
evidence: This is inferred from the different patterns of calcium responses to odor vs sugar.

claim: The local control of PAM presynaptic activity by GABA-B-R3 regulates odor responses, possibly by refining its spatial representation.
source: These results suggest that the local control of PAM presynaptic activity by GABA-B-R3 regulates the odor responses, possibly by refining its spatial representation.
evidence: This is inferred from the altered odor responses and spatial patterns upon GABA-B-R3 knockdown.

claim: There is no clear correlation between cluster size and intensity of pixels in the cluster.
source: Note that we did not observe a clear correlation between the cluster size and intensity of pixels in the cluster (data not shown), suggesting that the cluster size measure provides information orthogonal to the intensity value of calcium signals.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from data analysis, though data is not shown.

claim: Cluster size measure provides information orthogonal to the intensity value of calcium signals.
source: Note that we did not observe a clear correlation between the cluster size and intensity of pixels in the cluster (data not shown), suggesting that the cluster size measure provides information orthogonal to the intensity value of calcium signals.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of correlation between cluster size and intensity.

claim: Intense Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry signals are more spatially clustered in knock-down PAM terminals.
source: We further found that intense Brp::GCaMP6s::mCherry signals are more spatially clustered in the knock-down PAM terminals, further corroborating the fine spatial regulation of calcium signals by GABA-B-R3.
evidence: This is supported by peak size analysis mentioned in the text and supplementary figure.

claim: Overall disinhibition in knock-down terminals may impair selective delivery of dopaminergic reward signals to odor-activated KCs.
source: Since KC and PAM terminals form mutual synapses in the MB lobe (Takemura et al., 2017; Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2017), the overall disinhibition in the knock-down terminals may impair the selective delivery of dopaminergic reward signals to odor-activated KCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical connectivity and observed changes in spatial calcium patterns.

claim: In wild-type flies, local modulation of PAM activity is restricted to PAM synapses onto odor-activated KCs.
source: In wild-type flies, this local modulation is restricted to the PAM synapses onto the odor-activated KCs, which laterally inhibit activities of surrounding ones via KC-APL (anterior paired lateral) feedback.
evidence: This is part of the model presented in Figure 4E based on the experimental findings.

claim: Odor-activated KCs laterally inhibit activities of surrounding KCs via KC-APL feedback.
source: In wild-type flies, this local modulation is restricted to the PAM synapses onto the odor-activated KCs, which laterally inhibit activities of surrounding ones via KC-APL (anterior paired lateral) feedback.
evidence: This is part of the model presented in Figure 4E based on the experimental findings and known circuitry.

claim: GABA-B-R3 knock-down in PAM neurons eliminates negative feedback from APL.
source: GABA-B-R3 knock-down in the PAM neurons eliminates this negative feedback from the APL, reducing the activity contrast within presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons and the selectivity of memory to the rewarded odor.
evidence: This is part of the model presented in Figure 4E explaining the mechanism of the observed effects.

claim: GABA-B-R3 knock-down reduces activity contrast within presynaptic terminals of PAM neurons.
source: GABA-B-R3 knock-down in the PAM neurons eliminates this negative feedback from the APL, reducing the activity contrast within presynaptic terminals of the PAM neurons and the selectivity of memory to the rewarded odor.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial calcium imaging data showing broader activation patterns.

claim: Reciprocal PAM-KC synapses serve as KC activity-dependent local enhancers for reward signaling from PAM synapses.
source: In an odor response, reciprocal PAM-KC (Kenyon cell) synapses serve as KC activity-dependent local enhancers for reward signaling from the PAM synapses.
evidence: This is part of the model presented in Figure 4E based on known anatomy and the experimental findings.

claim: Input sources of sugar and odor response to PAM neurons are different.
source: Note that input sources of sugar and odor response are different.
evidence: This is stated in the model description in Figure 4E and supported by the differential calcium responses in dendrites vs terminals.
